full_judgment:
2. Facts relevant for disposal of the Rule, in brief, are that the opposite party Nos. 1-7 as plaintiffs filed Other Class Suit No. 271 of 1979 before the 1st Munsif (now Assistant Judge) Satkania, Chittagong for declaration of title and partition against the petitioner and defendant-respondent opposite parties as defendants stating, inter-alia that the schedule property originally belonged to one Ahmed Ali by virtue of a patta dated 12-6-1890 and accordingly, CS Khatian stands recorded in his name. The said Ahmed Ali died leaving two sons namely; defendant No.1 and Azizur Rahman, the predecessor of defendant Nos. 1 to 4 and daughter, plaintiff No.2. According to law of inheritance each son got 2/5th share and the daughter got 1/5th share. During RS operation taking advantage of the minority of the heirs of CS recorded tenant i,e the claimant, Hasan Ali and others got their names recorded in RS Khatian collusively though they have/had no right, title, interest and possession in the suit property. On the basis of RS Khatian they having failed to enter into possession of the suit land, created some forged documents in favour of defendant Nos. 5-26. The claim of the plaintiffs in the schedule land is 1.64 acres out of 2.74 acres being 3/5th shares. The property in question has not yet been partitioned among the co-sharer. The defendants threatening the plaintiff with possession and as such, the plaintiff demanded partition of the property but the defendants refused to do so. Hence the suit. 

 6. Mr Md Mokbul Ahmed with Mr Md Mizanul Haque Chowdhury and Mr Samiul Huq, the learned Advocates appearing for the petitioner submit that the trial court passed the judgment and decree on consideration of the evidences both oral and documentary adduced on behalf of the parties to the suit and rightly found that the plaintiff-opposite parties utterly failed to prove their title in the property as well as possession of the same and as such, the judgment and decree of the appellate court not in accordance with law but contrary to the facts and circumstances of the case and by sending the case back on remand has committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. Mr Ahmed further submits that the plaintiff-opposite parties by adducing and producing any evidence could not prove that RS Khatian was wrongly recorded in the names of Hasan Ali and others. Moreover, the plaintiff opposite parties name also recorded in RS Khatian along with Hasan Ali and others as co-sharer. The plaintiff-opposite parties ought to have sought relief against the RS Khatian at least before publication of SA Khatian but the plaintiffs remained silent about the wrong recording of RS Khatian and awaited for a long time even upto publication of present BS Khatian, which is absolutely unusual and by this time the defendant-petitioner has acquired an indefeasible right, title, interest and possession in the suit property on the basis of auction purchase.
